question: Does a behavior-carrying hunk change how data or settings customers already saved are read, matched, or applied?
procedure:
YES if, for records customers created before this change -- saved
rules, filters, queries, settings, configuration, stored documents --
a hunk changes what the product does with them: a stored value or form
it no longer accepts or recognizes, a stored field now read with a
different meaning, default, or unit, or a saved rule that now matches
or applies to a different set of things. Cite the hunk and the code
that reads those records.

Handling of a form at merge_base is the evidence that records in that
form can exist: a hunk that removes or narrows it is YES without proof
of how many there are.

NO when only new writes change: validation that rejects bad input at
save time leaves records already saved as they were, unless the same
check also runs when they are read or applied. NO when the change adds
a new field or form and reads existing records exactly as before. NO
for a move, copy, or swap of stored records that keeps their values
and meaning -- a rebuilt table, a new index, a renamed physical table
behind the same logical name.

A record that was misread at merge_base and is now read as intended is
still YES: its behavior changes.
unresolved_when:
The stored records are written or read by a service outside the tree,
and the packet does not show whether the form the change drops or
reinterprets is one that service writes.
